heroHeadline: UN Issues High Alert on Sudan: 880 Civilians Killed by Drones Jan–Apr 2026; SAF Strikes Nyala Two Consecutive Days, Downs RSF Bayraktar Akıncı UCAV
heroSubtitle: On Day 1122, UN Human Rights Chief Volker Türk issued a 'high alert' on widening conflict in Sudan, reporting that at least 880 civilians were killed and more than 770 injured by drone strikes between January and April 2026 — with drone attacks accounting for over 80% of all conflict-related civilian deaths. Türk cited May 8 RSF drone strikes on Al Quz (South Kordofan) and near El Obeid (North Kordofan) that killed 26 civilians as among the most recent examples, and warned of imminent further escalation. Civilian markets were targeted at least 28 times and health facilities 12+ times in this period. Simultaneously, SAF launched drone strikes on Nyala, South Darfur for a second consecutive day (May 10–11), striking central Nyala, the international airport, and the Al-Riyadh neighborhood — SAF claims 240 RSF vehicles destroyed and hundreds of RSF fighters killed. SAF Air Defense Forces reported downing an RSF-operated Baykar Bayraktar Akıncı UCAV over Nyala Airport on May 11 — the most capable Turkish drone system yet reported in RSF hands, suggesting continued advanced drone supply via Turkey-UAE networks. Earlier on May 10, Tarco Aviation and Sudanair completed the restoration of multi-carrier service to Khartoum International Airport, 10 days after the RSF/UAE drone attack forced a four-day closure, while Sudan's Civil Aviation Authority reported cumulative aviation revenue losses exceeding $1 billion since April 2023. Sudan's civil war enters Day 1122 with 14 million displaced, 880+ civilians killed by drones in four months, 34 million in urgent humanitarian need, the 2026 UN appeal only 16% funded, and no ceasefire framework in sight.
